clue.text: Story should be read for instance in advance

indicators.note: the words for instance sit in the word for advance, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: to advance money is to lend it
EG, short for exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: A tale that ought to be read ahead of time, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be read' is a nod to the Latin root of the answer, legenda, things to be read, and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional tale handed down, such as one of King Arthur, is a story of this kind.

clue.text: Part of W country river re-channelled, or one carrying it out ?

parts.note: the Exe flows through Devon in England's West Country
a cut is an artificial channel dug for water

explanation.surface: A stretch of a Devon river diverted, or the engineer doing the work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' joins the river to its CUT. The definition hints at a will: the person named to carry out its terms.
explanation.definitionFit: The person appointed to carry out a will's instructions holds this title.

clue.text: How can one make top sleep? (gag in court)

indicators.note: asks how a new word could be made by rearranging the letters of top sleep

explanation.surface: A puzzle about sending a spinning toy to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A legal rule barring someone from denying what they earlier asserted acts as a courtroom muzzle.

clue.text: Heredity factors among debt-collectors in Kent

genes are the units of heredity

explanation.surface: Inherited traits found among bailiffs in the south-east of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A shingle headland with a nuclear power station on the coast of Kent, the county in south-east England.

clue.text: Up the pole? But they were highly regarded

definitions.text: Up the pole? But they were highly regarded

parts.words: Up the pole? But they were highly regarded

explanation.definitionFit: Pillar saints such as Simeon spent years perched on columns, venerated by crowds below.

clue.text: Band-wagon in new Class I Motorcade

explanation.surface: A first-class motorcade with a bandwagon in it.

clue.text: Permission to view?

parts.note: in Britain you need a paid permit to watch television, which reads like permission to look at anything

explanation.definitionFit: A British TV permit is a formal permit to watch broadcasts, required by law.

clue.text: Fabulous racer killed Aeschylus

definitions.meaning: in Aesop's fable a slow reptile beats the hare in a race
legend says an eagle dropped a shelled reptile on the bald head of the Greek playwright Aeschylus

explanation.surface: A legendary runner who murdered a Greek tragedian.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow shelled reptile of Aesop's race, and the creature dropped by an eagle on Aeschylus.

clue.text: Team not assumed to be, of star quality

parts.note: a side is a team
real means genuine, not assumed or pretended

explanation.surface: A team that is genuinely full of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the stars, as in astronomy's star-based time.

clue.text: German heads of the European Union, note

indicators.note: the heads of three words are their opening letters

parts.note: the tonic is the keynote of a musical scale

explanation.surface: German leaders of the EU take note.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes the Germanic peoples and things German.

clue.text: Won points in science or education

parts.note: SC is a standard abbreviation for science

explanation.surface: Someone earned marks in a science or education exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To win points in a game is to have notched them up on the board.

clue.text: So Ena, outside disorderly pub, gets a summons

indicators.note: the name So Ena stands outside, wrapping the jumbled pub

parts.note: taken as written, the words so and Ena run together

indicators.note: something disorderly is in a mess, so the letters of pub are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ena, of soap opera fame, is served a writ after a rowdy night at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena Sharples was a famous character in the British soap Coronation Street, which makes the pub scene apt; 'disorderly' and 'outside' are the two signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ ordering someone to attend court is a legal summons.

clue.text: No open events in these games ?

definitions.text: No open events in these games ?

parts.words: No open events in these games ?
parts.note: open here means open to all comers, but read again it means outdoors: games under a roof have no open-air events

explanation.definitionFit: Sports such as darts or squash are played under cover rather than in the open air.

clue.text: Bathsheba always goes to the valley

parts.note: ever means always
a dene is a small wooded valley

explanation.surface: The biblical Bathsheba is forever heading down to the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Bathsheba looks biblical, but she is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Far from the Madding Crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardy's farmer heroine bears this surname as her family name.

clue.text: The bloom of youth

explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil family's flower is named after the beautiful youth of myth.

clue.text: Dentist's examination ?

parts.note: a test done by speaking rather than writing, and also what a dentist does, examine the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, and also something concerning the mouth, which a dentist inspects.

clue.text: Sporting leap year celebration

parts.note: the modern Games fall every four years, coinciding with leap years, and leap suggests jumping events

clue.text: The last such resolution would be in elementary terms

clue.text: Bull or cow that makes an impression

definitions.meaning: male and female marine mammals are called bull and cow

clue.text: " Grate on their pipes of wretched straw " (Milton)

clue.text: Curing lame stag was Ptolemy's work

clue.text: Atomically the same but different, is epically 'uge

clue.text: Canine neighbour is a biter

taken as written
